content:
Let's begin with the most fundamental vector operation: vector addition. Imagine vectors as arrows in space, each with a direction and length. Adding two vectors means placing the tail of the second vector at the head of the first and drawing a new arrow from the start of the first to the end of the second. This new arrow represents their sum.

This geometric view helps because vector addition corresponds to combining directions and magnitudes. In high-dimensional spaces, although we can't visualize easily, the same rules apply: each vector has components along each dimension, and addition happens component-wise.

To check your intuition: If you add a vector pointing east to one pointing north, what direction does their sum point?
